source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A lost forest at night: giant trunks, fireflies drifting between them, a forest that has forgotten its old songs and quietly moves its paths. Gentle wonder with a thread of unease, never scary. A breathy wooden flute sings a modal D-minor melody over a patient harp and marimba pattern; soft hand percussion walks like careful footsteps. Tempo 92 BPM, 4/4 time, key of D minor. Instrumentation: wooden flute lead, concert harp, marimba and kalimba droplets, soft hand percussion (frame drum, shaker), warm low strings, a clarinet answer in the second section. Form: 4-bar harp and kalimba intro; section A flute melody; section B clarinet and strings take a new, more yearning melody in F major; a sparse interlude of marimba and fireflies-like kalimba; section A returns with fuller strings; the last bar leads back to section A. Duration: 125 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
